title: Encapsulation & Abstraction
summary: Teaches the difference between class attributes (shared by every object) and instance attributes (unique to one object), and the three kinds of methods: instance methods (self), class methods (@classmethod, cls) and static methods (@staticmethod). Step-by-step guide arrives when the lecture is published.
goal: Decide whether data belongs on the class or on each instance, and pick the right method type for a behavior.

steps.title: Read the two lecture pages
steps.detail: Read 'Class vs Instance Attributes' and 'Class, Instance, and Static Methods' on the curriculum page. Pay attention to the 'attribute shadowing' gotcha.
steps.doneWhen: You can explain class attribute, instance attribute and attribute shadowing in one sentence each.

steps.title: Run the shared counter example
steps.detail: Save this as oop2_practice.py in a scratch folder (not inside an assignment repo) and run it with python3. It is the curriculum's population counter plus the shadowing gotcha.
steps.code:
class Person:
    species = "Human"
    population = 0

    def __init__(self, name, age):
        self.name = name
        self.age = age
        Person.population += 1

p1 = Person("Alice", 25)
p2 = Person("Bob", 30)
print(Person.population)

p1.species = "Mutant"   # creates an instance attribute
print(p1.species)
print(Person.species)
steps.doneWhen: It prints 2, then Mutant, then Human.

steps.title: Try a class method and a static method
steps.detail: Add these two methods inside the Person class (indented under it, above the p1 = line). A class method builds a new object from a string; a static method is a plain helper that lives in the class.
steps.doneWhen: Person.from_string("Alice, 25").age prints 25 and Person.greet("Bob") prints Hello Bob.

concepts.meaning: Data stored on one object through self, like self.name.
Data defined on the class itself and shared by every object, like a counter.
Assigning self.x when the class has x creates a new instance copy instead of changing the shared one.
A method marked @classmethod that receives the class (cls), often used to build new objects.
A method marked @staticmethod that gets neither self nor cls; a helper grouped with the class.
